March 8, 2025. Decomposed granite (DG) is a versatile and cost-effective material commonly used for driveways, pathways, patios, and landscaping projects. However, not all DG is the same. Two of the most popular types are washed decomposed granite and screened decomposed granite. Understanding the differences between these types will help you choose the best material for your project.
What is Washed Decomposed Granite?

Washed DG undergoes a cleaning process that removes fine particles and dust, leaving behind clean, uniform 1/4-inch granite granules. This process enhances its drainage properties and provides a smoother finish. Key Features of Washed DG: Dust-Free & Cleaner Finish – Ideal for decorative landscaping. Excellent Drainage – Perfect for areas with heavy rain or runoff. Less Compaction – Remains loose and permeable.
Best Uses for Washed DG:

Best Uses for Washed DG: French drains and drainage systems. Loose-fill pathways with minimal dust. Decorative landscaping in xeriscaping projects. Top dressing around plants for aesthetic appeal. Pro Tip: Washed DG is great for Arizona’s monsoon season, as it prevents excessive dust buildup and improves water filtration.
What is Screened Decomposed Granite?

Screened DG is processed to remove large pieces while retaining smaller fines and dust, allowing for better compaction and a more stable surface. Unlike washed DG, this type binds together, creating a firmer, more compact surface ideal for driveways and high-traffic areas. Key Features of Screened DG: Compacts Well – Great for creating solid, stable surfaces. Better for Driveways & Walkways – Reduces shifting and erosion. Provides a Natural Look – Blends seamlessly into landscapes.
Best Uses for Screened DG:

Best Uses for Screened DG: Driveways and high-traffic walkways. Patios and seating areas. Base material for pavers or flagstone. Erosion control on slopes and hillsides. Pro Tip: If you’re looking for the best decomposed granite for driveways, screened DG is the best choice due to its compactability and durability.
Washed vs. Screened DG – Which One Should You Choose?

Need a dust-free, permeable option with excellent drainage? → Go with Washed DG. Need a firm, compact surface for driveways or pathways? → Screened DG is your best bet. April 26, 2025. When it comes to landscaping in Arizona, decorative rock isn’t just a design choice — it’s a smart solution built for the desert heat, water conservation, and low-maintenance living. At ABC Sand & Rock, we’ve helped hundreds of Arizona homeowners find the right materials to create beautiful, lasting landscapes. And after years of working with real families and contractors, we’ve seen what works best. If you’re planning to refresh your yard, here are our top 5 decorative rock ideas we recommend for Arizona homes:
Crushed Granite Pathways

We’ve seen crushed granite become a favorite for homeowners who want their yards to look natural but feel polished. Its warm, earthy colors blend perfectly with native plants like agave and mesquite. Pro Tip: If you’re dreaming of a clean, easy-to-walk path, go for a 1/4″ minus crushed granite. It compacts beautifully underfoot and holds up well to Arizona’s intense sun and flash storms.
River Rock Garden Beds

Picture this: smooth, rounded river rocks surrounding your desert plants, reflecting soft shades of tan, rust, and gray. River rock creates a calming, natural flow through garden beds and tree wells — plus it helps regulate soil temperature, saving moisture where it matters most. If you’re aiming for a yard that looks effortless but stays resilient, river rock is a go-to choice.
Rip Rap for Erosion Control and Bold Design

Have a sloped yard or an area that struggles with heavy rain? Rip rap — large, angular stone — doesn’t just hold the ground together; it looks stunning when paired with dramatic desert plants like barrel cactus and ocotillo. We often recommend rip rap when customers want something functional and rugged, but still eye-catching.
Pea Gravel Courtyards

Pea gravel is one of those hidden gems in desert landscaping. It’s perfect for creating cozy courtyards, firepit hangouts, or meditation spaces right at home. Imagine a smooth, cool surface underfoot, shaded by a desert willow — pea gravel turns outdoor spaces into inviting, casual retreats. Plus, it’s great for keeping the ground cooler during Arizona’s hottest months.
Desert Gold Decorative Rock

Nothing says “Arizona” quite like Desert Gold rock. Its bright, sunny hues instantly brighten up front yards, patios, and desert gardens. It’s a customer favorite here at ABC Sand & Rock because it holds its color even in brutal summer heat. Red Cinder is a naturally lightweight volcanic rock with a deep burgundy-to-rust color that comes from the iron oxide in the original lava flow. Color reads as a warm brick red in direct sun, with darker maroon and the occasional charcoal or natural stone fleck mixed in. Lightweight: easier on raised planters, rooftops, and any application where load matters. Doesn’t compact: won’t pack down into a hardened layer the way some decomposed granites will.
